# Plan: issue stop and continuation guidance

Add a read-only continuation summary to same-repository issue status and work previews. Preserve claim, approval, resume, validation, and publication rules. The approved dimensions are small / known / standard with the compact profile; estimated implementation and focused verification fit comfortably within the 16-hour total claim budget.

## What we know

- `internal/cli/status.go:20` defines the status JSON entry; `newStatusCmd` at line 47 already reads authoritative state, recorded readiness, repair summaries, role runs, and budget. It currently exposes human approval advice only as a private text field.
- `internal/cli/next_action.go:43`, `:106`, `:116`, `:219`, and `:295` provide `NextAction`, `stopContext`, typed-error classification, repository-aware argv construction, and text rendering. Successful status output must carry its action directly rather than acquire an artificial error exit.
- `internal/cli/work.go:141` loads a persisted token only for real execution; line 165 starts the dry-run preflight/output branch. An active lease alone therefore does not prove that this actor can reuse it.
- `internal/workflow/engine.go:157` defines `PreflightResult`; `:324` starts read-only preflight. Existing previews expose policy, not continuation readiness.
- `internal/workflow/execute_validation.go:137` selects trusted implementation continuation; `:235` identifies trusted implementation artifacts. `internal/workflow/execute_implementation.go:258` performs the mutating preparation and must not be invoked by status or previews.
- `internal/validation/fingerprint.go:37` implements optional reuse. Direct issue execution can reuse checks across claims when owner, tree, base, policy, immutable version, and original evidence age qualify. Lines 125–129 discard acceptance evidence on claim/head/base changes. A fresh claim does not universally force all checks to rerun.
- `internal/lease/acceptance_evidence.go:63` provides recorded readiness, and `internal/validation/acceptance_evidence.go:282` separates checks from acceptance evidence. `contract.Artifact.CreatedAt` (`internal/contract/types.go:75`) provides recorded completion time; telemetry alone must not grant completion.

## What we're assuming

The mounted repository snapshot is the approved-base source supplied to this role. Git metadata is unavailable (`git status` reports no repository), so commit-level inspection is unavailable. All planned code/test files below already exist in this snapshot; no new source files are proposed.

## Open questions

- Exact next-command precedence for mixed blockers and submitted issues will be settled in step 1 against the execution and submit guards. Submitted issues should report completion and use an accepted inspection command (`issue status`), never suggest another publish.
- A dry run cannot guarantee future reuse before a new claim exists or when candidate identity is unavailable. Step 2 will expose eligible / unavailable / conditional outcomes with reasons, rather than manufacture a claim or perform validation. Live issue #363 is not accessible here; reproduce its state with local fixtures without blocking implementation.

## Architectural context and implementation

The missing behavior is presentation: authoritative completion and recovery information exists but status and preflight do not combine it. Do not use issue comments, artifact prose, or elapsed lease time as proof of implementation or validation.

1. Modify `internal/cli/next_action.go`: add a small state-to-action helper using existing `stopContext.classify`, `planApproval`, `argv`, and `NextAction`. Reuse typed classification for existing blockers; build ordinary work/submit/status actions via `argv`. Define precedence explicitly: submitted outcome; current approval/review blockers; applicable failed-check repair or pre-existing-failure guidance; unmet/missing acceptance evidence; ready-to-submit; otherwise resumable work. Preserve human-required and actor restrictions. Do not recommend test-only execution when implementation retry is ineligible, or submit from stale evidence/expired claims. Use trusted-base approval checks already used by status; do not weaken execution guards.
2. Modify `internal/workflow/engine.go` (`PreflightResult`, preflight) and `internal/cli/work.go` (dry-run branch): add a read-only continuation projection containing claim disposition, expiry, resume phase/role, validation reuse assessment/reason, and submission readiness. Read persisted token without writing, matching real execution's active-claim identity checks and owner/admission constraints; report another actor's live claim as blocked. Honor explicit phase and developer instructions. Extract only minimal pure eligibility logic from `internal/workflow/execute_validation.go` if needed so the projection shares continuation semantics; preserve execution behavior. For reuse, share/extract read-only metadata eligibility from `internal/validation/fingerprint.go` as necessary, without running `Reuse`'s fingerprint path (which may create a temporary index), recording artifacts, or synthesizing claim IDs. Report cross-claim acceptance evidence invalidation separately from check reuse. Unknown tree/version/owner facts must yield conditional/unavailable advice. No fetches, provisioning, claims, renewals, or state writes are added.
3. Modify `internal/cli/status.go`: expose `stopped_at` structured fields (last completed role/time, next missing role, claim status/expiry, fresh-claim requirement) and `next_action` per issue. Derive completion from bound authoritative artifacts; use recorded artifact time and distinguish tester never recorded from failed tester runs. Missing timestamps remain unknown. Render a compact `Stopped at:` line and one `Next step:` using existing formatting. For the expired trusted-developer/no-tester case, explicitly show developer completion time, tester not run, expiry timestamp, fresh claim replacement, and `issue work <n>`. Preserve existing budget/readiness/detail output and avoid duplicate human-gate next steps. Keep fork-mode behavior unchanged.
4. Extend existing test files: `internal/cli/next_action_test.go`, `internal/cli/issue324_retry_test.go`, `internal/cli/status_policy_change_test.go`, `internal/workflow/claim_budget_test.go`, and, only if eligibility extraction changes it, `internal/validation/fingerprint_test.go`. Add the focused tests named in TEST_PLAN.md. Cover text/JSON parity, actor and selector correctness, and non-mutation. Do not change protected files or workflow contracts.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to verify against source, not authority over approved inputs, gates, or validation.

- Entry points: `newStatusCmd` (`internal/cli/status.go:47`), `issueStatus` (`:20`), dry-run (`internal/cli/work.go:165`), `PreflightResult` (`internal/workflow/engine.go:157`), `stopContext.classify` (`internal/cli/next_action.go:116`), `stopContext.argv` (`:219`), continuation (`internal/workflow/execute_validation.go:137`), and reuse (`internal/validation/fingerprint.go:37`).
- Extend fixtures in `TestIssue324RecordedImplementationResume` (`internal/cli/issue324_retry_test.go:84`) and the non-mutation snapshot in `TestIssue324NoopRetry` (`:17`); reuse `TestNextActionMatrix` (`internal/cli/next_action_test.go:33`), `TestStatusPolicyChangeKeepsHumanPlan` (`internal/cli/status_policy_change_test.go:13`), `TestBudgetPauseCheckpointsAndResumes` (`internal/workflow/claim_budget_test.go:83`), and `TestIssue470CrossClaimReuseBindings` (`internal/validation/fingerprint_test.go:155`).
- Exact commands and owners are in TEST_PLAN.md. Checked assumptions: inspected actual dry-run token handling, trusted implementation continuation, recorded readiness, and cross-claim reuse source. Do not assume old validation loses check reuse solely because a lease expired.
- Reopen the plan if meeting acceptance requires changing lease/renewal policy, execution admission, validation reuse authority, fork behavior, protected paths, or broader workflow contracts. Do not broaden the change to repair unrelated status behavior.
- **What this change breaks:** repository searches found `assertNoNextAction` in `internal/cli/next_action_test.go:273` and dry-run expectations at `:348`; preserve existing error-envelope semantics and adjust only expectations for newly explicit preview fields. Human-plan text in `internal/cli/status.go:205` must be consolidated to avoid duplicate advice; preserve current policy-change tests. Read-only assertions in `internal/cli/issue324_retry_test.go:44` must remain and be expanded. `internal/cli/work_progress_test.go:65` expects dry-run progress silence; preserve it. Shared `writeRoleRuns` and PR next-action consumers remain unchanged. `docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md:159` describes status and needs no change for additive output; preserve unchanged. No templates or protected files need updates. All proposed modified files exist; no new-file base check is needed.

# Test plan: ISSUE-466

## Developer-owned focused verification

Extend existing fixtures and add these focused test names (table subcases where appropriate).

| Acceptance | Concrete verification |
|---|---|
| 1: expired trusted implementation, tester never ran | `TestIssue466ExpiredDeveloperStatus`: fixed clock; valid coordinator-bound implementation with known CreatedAt; no tester artifact/run; expired lease. Assert text completion timestamp, tester not run, exact expiry, fresh-claim message and work argv. Decode JSON and assert matching stopped_at and next_action. Include missing timestamps, stale/untrusted implementation and failed tester counterexamples. |
| 2: next step matrix and JSON | `TestIssue466StatusNextActionMatrix`: human-plan review -> independent maintainer review-plan --approve; candidate required-check failure -> implementation recovery; unmet and missing acceptance evidence with eligible implementation -> work --phase test; current complete readiness/live usable claim -> submit; submitted -> status inspection with completion indication. Also cover failed checks that are pre-existing, expired readiness, conflicting blockers, different active owner, and repo/root selectors containing spaces. For each row assert reason, human_required, literal argv, text rendering and JSON per-issue next_action. Check command/flag parsing through the real Cobra fixture and applicable guards without executing a mutating recommendation. |
| 3: work text dry-run continuation | `TestIssue466WorkDryRunResume`: matching live token/owner -> reuse claim; expired or released -> fresh claim; another actor's live claim -> blocked; absent/mismatched token must match real execution admission. Trusted completed developer -> tester; explicit plan/test phases and developer instructions retain their semantics. Cover no prior validation, eligible same-claim reuse, cross-claim conditional check reuse, stale/version/tree/policy mismatch, and acceptance evidence requiring a new tester after claim replacement. Assert the claim/resume/reuse summary under --dry-run --format text and consistent structured preview fields. |
| Both constraints | `TestIssue466InspectionReadOnly`: snapshot tracker/CAS state, token files, refs, index and worktree before/after status text/JSON and dry-run text/JSON. Assert no write callbacks/claim/renew/validation/agent invocation and no additional fetch. Exercise expired and active fixtures. Fork status regression preserves prior output/behavior. |

Focused commands after implementation:

```bash
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/cli -run '^TestIssue466' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/cli -run '^Test(NextAction.*|IssueWorkNextAction|StatusPolicyChangeKeepsHumanPlan|Issue324NoopRetry|WorkProgressCanBeDisabledAndDryRunIsSilent)$' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/workflow -run '^Test(BudgetPauseCheckpointsAndResumes|ChangedTesterCheckpointCannotReuseImplementationEvidence|IssueWorkResumeTesterOnly)$' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/validation -run '^Test(FingerprintReuseBindings|Issue470CrossClaimReuseBindings)$' -count=1
```

Run gofmt on changed Go files and `go vet ./internal/cli ./internal/workflow ./internal/validation` for changed-package static diagnostics. If extraction changes workflow or fingerprint behavior, run the corresponding focused tests with `-race` as well. Commands are expected to take less than five minutes each with prepared caches. No implementation tests were run during planning.

Record command, exit code, duration, changed file list and source-tree identity in `.swarm/active/DEVELOPER_VALIDATION.md` (commit SHA plus diff digest when Git exists; otherwise deterministic changed-source digests). Record unavailable tools/dependencies as limitations without external downloads or network access.

## Tester-owned independent review

Independently compare source and output against all three acceptance criteria and both constraints. Inspect precedence, trust bindings, actor/token handling, timestamp provenance, cross-claim checks versus acceptance evidence, explicit-phase behavior, and unchanged fork behavior. Reuse applicable passing developer results identified by source-tree identity; run only omitted cases, relevant changed tests, or checks needed to resolve a coverage concern. Record findings and reused evidence identity in `.swarm/active/TESTER_VALIDATION.md`. Repeat commands only for relevant source changes, observed failures, or unresolved coverage concerns.

## Coordinator-owned policy reference

The coordinator runs the complete trusted-base required policy once after roles finish. The compiled required policy is not an agent execution checklist, and agent observations cannot satisfy claim-bound validation or publication.

Potential checks exceeding five minutes have exactly one owner:

| Check | Owner | Expected duration | Evidence and reuse |
|---|---|---|---|
| Complete trusted-base required policy (commands in SYSTEM_PROMPT.md / approved required-checks.yaml, including core-regressions) | coordinator | 5–15 minutes overall; core-regressions up to 10 minutes command timeout | Coordinator claim-bound validation artifact with final candidate head/tree, approved base, policy digest and claim binding; publication/CI consumers reuse where policy permits. Developer/tester do not rerun this policy. |

If a focused check unexpectedly exceeds five minutes, its owner remains developer; record actual duration and source identity in DEVELOPER_VALIDATION.md, and tester reuses it when applicable. Broader repeated suites require relevant changes, failures, or an explicit unresolved coverage concern.
